chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad who said: Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated to me, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say:

Seven people spoil their deeds: 1. The patient man with abundant knowledge who is not known for it and is not mentioned because of it; 2. The wise man who entrusts his wealth to every liar who denies what is given to him; 3. The man who trusts those of deceit and treachery; 4. The harsh master who has no mercy; 5. The mother who does not keep secrets from her children and reveals them to them; 6. The one who is quick to blame his companions; 7. The one who continually argues with his brother in a contentious manner.
ai.seo_question: What are the seven things that spoil a Muslim's deeds according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq identifies seven internal and external vices that corrupt spiritual merit, emphasizing that hidden knowledge and unacknowledged wisdom are as destructive as overt hypocrisy. This list highlights the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and *hilm* (forbearance) in social interactions, warning against the subtle erosion of faith through harshness, secrecy, and contentiousness. The inclusion of the mother revealing secrets underscores the domestic sphere as a critical site for maintaining trust and dignity within the family unit.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-23 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Abdullah al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Abi Uthman, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hilal, on the authority of Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi that he had heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say,

“The following seven people spoil their deeds.1- A wise highly knowledgeable man who doesn’t teach his knowledge to the people and is unknown to the extent that nobody mentions his name2- A wise man who entrusts his wealth to wicked liars who would not return it to him3- Those who trust mischievous and disloyal people4- Noble people who are not compassionate to others5- Mothers who do not protect the secrets of their offspring and divulge them6- Those who rush to blame their companions and brethren7- Those who continually quarrel with their colleagues and brethren.”
